title: The Pro Audio Spectrum's I/O registers
covers: the offsets from the Pro Audio Spectrum's 388h base that DOSBox-X decodes: the interrupt, filter, PCM, 8253 timer, MIDI, board-identification, configuration and Sound Blaster emulation registers, as Media Vision's 1992 Developer's Toolkit Reference describes the common ones and as the emulator handles them

searched.gave: MAME has no Pro Audio Spectrum device; its tree names no datasheet for the card.
Media Vision was bought out; the 1992 Developer's Toolkit Reference was found in PASSDK_201.zip, and its state table names B88h the audio mixer control without a bit layout.
The Media Vision directory holds the SDK archive and no MV508 or board register document.
Searches for the Pro Audio Spectrum returned drivers, books and the toolkit, no register manual.
datasheetarchive-like indexes answered with sound cards and no MV508 mixer or board register document.

rows.text: The later models (Plus, 16 and CDPC) relocate their I/O addresses, so up to four boards can share a PC.
The card's 16-bit addressing scheme places OPL3 FM at 388h, MIDI at 1788h, SCSI at 5388h and configuration at F388h.
The original Pro Audio Spectrum used 388h through 38Bh as its base address.
Relocation can select any of 256 addresses; Media Vision recommends 388h, 384h, 38Ch or 288h.
The hardware must be reset before it accepts a new base address.
A relocation writes two bytes to 9A01h: the board ID BCh through BFh, then the base address shifted right by two.
The toolkit's own example sets the base to 388h by writing BCh and then 388h shifted right by two.
The procedure can be repeated for the next three boards.
The write handler at fixed port 0x9A01 is installed in the init branch that runs for the Plus and the 16.
The first byte is the board ID and the second, only after BCh was written, the new base; IDs BDh through BFh are stored and ignored.
The new base is kept and applied later, when a write to 0x8000 resets the board and reinstalls the ports.
B89h is the interrupt status register.
An interrupt service routine reads it to find which of the enabled interrupts needs servicing.
Bit D7 reports sample clipping; it is set automatically when the input is too loud and reset to 0 after each use.
Bit D6 reports the reset state, and is valid only on the older models, being reserved on the Plus, 16 and CDPC.
Bit D5 tells the left from the right PCM channel in stereo mode and stays 0 in mono mode.
Bit D4 reports an active MIDI controller interrupt.
Bit D3 reports the sample buffer count interrupt, which the programmer clears by writing a 0 to the register.
Bit D2 reports the sample rate timer interrupt, cleared by writing a 0 to the register.
Bit D1 reports the right FM interrupt, redefined on the Plus, 16 and CDPC.
Bit D0, which the scan prints as D1, reports the left FM interrupt, reset by acknowledging it.
Writing a 0 to the register clears the sample buffer count and sample rate timer interrupt bits.
The read masks D5 off, so the PCM left/right flag always reads 0.
The write clears the status bits written as 1 and drops the IRQ when none is left, always on the original; an unmute rise there clears the enables and status.
The buffer count interrupt is raised by the buffer counter, the tick sets or clears the left/right flag, and the PCM reset clears both.
The MIDI interrupt bit is raised when output mode meets status bits 4-3, input mode meets bit 2, or the YM3802 timer fires.
The board reset and the YM3802 reset clear the status bits.
Offset 0x2401 is the board revision register.
A read returns 0x00 on every board type.
B8Ah is the audio filter control register.
It sets bit masks that enable and disable counters, generate interrupts, mute and reset the board, and select filtering.
Bit D7 gates the sample buffer count register.
Bit D6 gates the sample rate timer register.
Bit D5 mutes the card: at 1 every source is mixed and output, at 0 only the PC speaker sounds.
Bits D4 through D0 select one of six low-pass filter rates from 17.897 kHz to 2.982 kHz, each with a 20 Hz low end.
A write sets the gate, mute and filter bits.
A read returns the byte last written.
The write clears the stereo and byte-order flips, resets the timer when D6 rises and the counter when D7 rises, and on the original clears interrupts when D5 rises.
The write renders the audio first, then updates the filter and the PCM channel.
The board reset clears the filter byte.
F88h is the PCM data register.
A read takes a sample from the analog-to-digital converter.
A write sends a sample to the digital-to-analog converter; all eight bits are programmed as a group.
The register serves direct-mode transfers only, not non-DMA PCM.
A read of this offset yields 0xFF on every board type.
A write stores nothing and returns.
F8Ah is the cross channel control register.
It manages the PCM hardware and DMA interface and configures the connections between the mixers.
Bit D7 enables the card's DMA circuitry and must be set before the PC's DMA controller is programmed.
Bit D6 enables the PCM state machine, after the sample timer is initialized.
Bit D5 selects stereo, where the first byte is the left channel and the second the right, or mono.
Bit D4 selects output (DAC) mode or input (ADC) mode.
Bit D3 connects the left input mixer output to the left output mixer input.
Bit D2 connects the right input mixer output to the left output mixer input.
Bit D1 connects the left input mixer output to the right output mixer input.
Bit D0 connects the right input mixer output to the right output mixer input.
A write sets the DMA enable, the PCM enable, the stereo select and the DAC or ADC select, and configures the mixer connections.
A reset clears every bit of the register.
A read returns the byte last written.
The write stores the byte and updates the channel; D6 with the gate and timer starts the PCM machine, D5 makes it mono, and D7 gates a DMA read.
B8Bh is the interrupt control register.
It enables feature interrupts and reports the hardware revision.
Bits D7 through D5 are a read-only field holding the hardware revision level.
Bit D4 enables the MIDI controller interrupt.
Bit D3 enables the sample buffer count interrupt.
Bit D2 enables the sample rate timer interrupt.
Bit D1 enables the right FM interrupt on the older models and is redefined on the Plus, 16 and CDPC.
Bit D0, printed as D O, enables the left FM interrupt.
A write sets the five interrupt enable bits D4 through D0.
A read returns the enable byte on the original, and that byte with bit 5 set on the Plus and 16.
The board reset clears the interrupt enables and the status bits.
1388h is the sample rate timer.
It sets the interval between PCM samples, so the card processes a sample and then waits that period.
A write programs all 16 bits of the interval.
For stereo sampling the timer is loaded with half the mono interval, since twice as many samples are needed.
The interval is 1,193,180 divided by the sample rate, so 22,050 Hz gives 54.
Before programming, the timer is selected at 138Bh and the B8Ah sample rate timer gate is cleared to 0.
A read returns the counter's value or the byte the control word's read mode selects.
The emulator renders the audio first, so a change lands at the right sample.
The read and write cases for the three timer offsets share one arm that passes the offset's low bits to the timer.
1389h is the sample buffer count.
It holds the 16-bit number of bytes in a DMA buffer division, halved on a 16-bit DMA channel.
A write programs the count; when it reaches zero a sample buffer count interrupt fires.
The count is selected at 138Bh and the B8Ah sample buffer counter gate is cleared before it is programmed.
The counter counts DMA transfers, not bytes, and fires only while PCM is enabled and the D3 interrupt is enabled.
The read and write cases for the three timer offsets share one arm that passes the offset's low bits to the timer.
138Ah is the local speaker timer count.
It shadows the PC speaker timer, and with the card installed PC speaker sounds are generated from it instead of from the PC.
A write programs the eight-bit speaker count of a PC-compatible 8253 timer, in any of its six modes.
A write stores the reload, and a read returns that reload rather than a running count.
The read and write cases for the three timer offsets share one arm that passes the offset's low bits to the timer.
138Bh is the local timer control register.
It enables and disables the timers, sets their read and write modes, their generator modes and binary or BCD counting.
Bits D7 and D6 select the sample rate timer, the sample buffer counter or the local speaker timer.
Bits D5 and D4 enable the 16-bit timer, the least significant byte first; the scan's lines are scrambled.
Bits D3-D1 select the timer mode; the prose gives the sample timer square wave and the buffer counter rate generator, the table the reverse.
Bit D0 selects BCD counting, though binary is the normal setting.
A write selects a timer and sets its read and write mode, generator mode and counting mode.
The byte is an 8253 control word: D0 is accepted but counting stays binary, and selecting counter 3 for a read-back is ignored.
The write case passes the control byte to the 8253 control word.
1788h is the MIDI prescale register.
It sets the interval for MIDI timer interrupts: (N+1)/2 milliseconds for a programmed value N.
A MIDI timer interrupt is generated when the decreasing value wraps from zero to 255, enabled by bit D0 of the MIDI control register.
The register is optional and intended for special interrupts.
A write programs bits D7 through D0 as a group; FFh sets 128 ms and 01h sets 1 ms.
The second write switch's arms take 0x1401, 0x1403, 0x1402, 0x1802, 0x1800, 0x1801 and the configuration ports; 0x1400 has no arm, so a write stores nothing on the Plus and 16.
That arm stores the control byte and picks the UART direction from bits 4 through 2.
On the original PAS, a read of 0x1400 returns the YM3802 vector, bits 7-5 from register 0, bits 3-1 from the timer, bit 4 set when none is pending.
The MIDI timer event sets the interrupt vector to 0x0E and the status bit to 0x80.
The YM3802 reset clears the interrupt vector and the status byte.
The other write arms handle 0x1402 with 0x1802, 0x1800 and 0x1801.
1789h is the MIDI timer register.
It is read-only: its value decreases in two-millisecond steps and resets to zero when the MIDI prescale register is programmed.
The MIDI system interrupts when the timer wraps to zero or equals the MIDI compare time.
The document says to set bits D7 through D0 as a group, FFh for a current MIDI time of 128 ms and 01h for 1 ms.
A read returns the current MIDI time.
The Plus returns its MIDI control byte and the original its register-group byte; neither counts a MIDI time.
On the original a write stores the register-group byte, selects a bank from bits 0-3, and resets the YM3802 when 0x80 falls to 0x00.
On the Plus a write stores the control byte and picks the UART direction from bits 4 through 2.
178Ah is the MIDI data register.
It sends data to the transmitter FIFO and receives from the receiver FIFO, so bytes move in bursts.
A read retrieves a byte from the MIDI receiver FIFO.
A write sends a byte to the MIDI transmitter FIFO.
The Plus returns 0 unless the UART echoes the 0xAA loopback byte; the original returns its interrupt status byte.
The Plus stores the byte and sends it when the UART is in output mode, without a FIFO; the original keeps its UART data at 0x1802.
The MIDI timer event sets the status bit to 0x80 and the YM3802 reset clears the status and vector bytes.
178Bh is the MIDI control register.
It echoes input to output, resets the FIFO pointers and enables the half-empty, empty, input, compare and timestamp interrupts.
Bit D7 enables echoing of input to output; it defaults to 1.
Bit D6 resets the output FIFO pointer and must be cleared again at once.
Bit D5 resets the input FIFO pointer and must be cleared again at once; the scan prints it as D6.
Bit D4 enables the output FIFO half-empty interrupt.
Bit D3 enables the output FIFO empty interrupt.
Bit D2 enables the input data available interrupt.
Bit D1 enables the compare time interrupt.
Bit D0 enables the timestamp interrupt, generated when the MIDI timer wraps from FFh to 00h.
A write sets the echo, FIFO reset and interrupt enable bits.
The Plus stores the byte, resets both UART directions when bits 6 and 5 are set and picks the direction from bits 4-2; the original clears interrupts with it.
The Plus returns the control byte; the original returns 0xFF.
1B88h is the MIDI status register.
It reports frame errors, the two FIFO overruns and the five interrupt conditions; writing a bit to 0 clears it, and the overrun and frame error interrupts are always on.
Bit D7 reports a frame error.
Bit D6 reports an output FIFO overrun.
Bit D5 reports an input FIFO overrun.
Bit D4 reports an output FIFO half-empty interrupt.
Bit D3 reports an output FIFO empty interrupt; the scan labels its table D4.
Bit D2 reports an input data available interrupt; the scan labels its table D4.
Bit D1 reports a compare time interrupt; the scan labels its table D4.
Bit D0 reports a timestamp interrupt; the scan labels its table D4.
Writing a status bit to 0 clears it.
The Plus stores the byte and raises the MIDI interrupt from bits 4-2; the original keeps it as register data and raises it from its timer.
A read returns the stored status byte; the original returns 0xC0 when the bank is 5.
A read of 0x1402 in UART input mode clears bit 2 of the status byte.
1B89h is the MIDI FIFO count register.
It tells how many bytes fit in the output FIFO and how many have arrived in the input FIFO.
Bits D7 through D4 give the output FIFO space, where 0 means either 0 or 16 bytes; the toolkit advises writing only 15 bytes at a time.
Bits D3 through D0 give the received byte count, where 0 means either 0 or 16 bytes.
A read returns the two four-bit FIFO counts.
The Plus returns the byte last written at 0x1801, not two FIFO counts; the original returns its register's stored value.
On the original a write stores the byte as bank 8's register, where the high half of the timer sits and bit 7 starts it.
Offset 0x0403 is the MV508 mixer port of the PAS 16.
A write on a PAS 16 hands the byte to the mixer routine; on the other boards nothing happens.
In the mixer routine bit 7 selects a register index, and otherwise the value is masked and stored in bank 0, 1 or 2.
Offset 0x0800 is the audio mixer port.
A read returns 0xFF on the original and the Plus, and the stored mixer byte on the PAS 16.
On the PAS 16 a write stores the byte unless bit 0 is set; on the other boards the byte drives the serial mixer state machine.
The serial stream shifts IDENT, CLOCK and DATA through STROBE into the LMC1982 or LMC835, and bit 7 of the shifted word marks an address.
The port is installed for every board type in the 4-port block at base plus 0x800.
The board type is fixed at init, and the original's power-up mixer byte is the FM-split-off value.

rows.text: Offset 0xC01 is the second byte of the PCM data port.
A write at 0xC01 stores nothing; its case is shared with 0xC00 and only renders the audio.
Offset 0x4000 holds a timeout count.
A read returns the stored count.
A write stores the byte unchanged.
Offset 0x4001 holds a timeout status byte.
A read returns the stored status.
A write stores the byte with bit 7 cleared.
Offset 0x7C01 holds the enhanced SCSI register.
A read returns the stored byte with bit 0 forced to 0.
A write stores the byte unchanged.
Offset 0xBC00 holds the wait states byte.
A read returns the stored byte.
A write stores the byte unchanged.
Offset 0xBC02 holds the PCM clock prescale divider.
A read returns the stored divider.
A write stores the divider and updates the PCM channel at once.
The clock is 1,008,000 or 441,000 Hz divided by the divider while bit 1 of the configuration bytes is set.
The board reset clears the prescale divider.
Offset 0xEC03 reports the operation mode: bits 1-0 the CD interface, bit 2 stereo FM and bit 3 16-bit audio.
A read returns 0x0F on the PAS 16 and 0x07 on the original and the Plus.
The board type these values depend on is fixed when the ports are installed at init.
Offset 0xFC00 reports the board model.
A read returns 0x0C on the PAS 16 and 0x01 on the original and the Plus.
The board type these values depend on is fixed when the ports are installed at init.
Offset 0xFC03 reports the master mode: AT bus and XT or AT timing.
A read returns 0x31 on the PAS 16 and 0x11 on the original and the Plus.
The board type these values depend on is fixed when the ports are installed at init.
1B8Ah is the MIDI Compare Time register.
A write loads a compare value; an interrupt is generated when the MIDI timer count equals it, and bits D7 through D0 are programmed as a group.
Using the register is optional; the document says it is useful for generating special interrupts.
The document gives N/A as the register's default.
On the Plus and 16 a write stores the byte as MIDI data and sends it when the UART is set to output.
On the original PAS the offset is YM3802 register 6, banked by the register index; a write stores the byte in that bank.
Register 6 index 5 also sends the byte to MIDI when register 5's index 5 has bit 0 set.
A read returns the stored byte, except at index 3 where it returns 0; the source notes there is no MIDI input.
A read returns 0 unless the loopback value 0xAA is latched with control bit 2 set, and then clears status bit 2.
Offset 0x1803 is YM3802 register 7, one of the four registers banked by the register index.
A read returns the stored byte of register 7 in the selected bank.
A write stores the byte in register 7 of the selected bank.
On the Plus and 16 no case handles 0x1803, so a read reaches the fall-through 0xFF.
8389h is the Sample Size Configuration register.
A program writes the register to select the output sample compression ratio and 8- or 16-bit audio.
Bits D7 through D3 are reserved; the document says not to program them, as that gives unpredictable behaviour.
Bit D2 selects 8-bit audio when clear and 16-bit when set; the heading is printed as 8116-bit by the OCR.
Not all products support 16-bit audio; the MVGetHWVersion call tells which do.
Bits D1 and D0 select over-sampling of 1, 2 or 4 times: 00 is 1X, 01 is 2X and 11 is 4X.
The document gives 0 as the default of the D2 field and of the D1-D0 field.
A read returns the byte last written.
A write stores the byte; the sample fetch takes 8- or 16-bit audio from D2 when it runs.
DOSBox-X gives D4 the sign inversion of the sample and D3 a mask of its low four bits.
The two over-sampling bits are stored and read back; the sample fetch, quoted whole, never tests them.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns 0xFF.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns without storing.
Offset 0x8000 reads and writes element 0 of the four-byte system configuration array.
A read returns the byte last written to it.
A write stores the byte, unless bits 7 and 6 rise from clear.
Bits 7 and 6 rising from clear reset the board, move the ports to the base stored at 0x9A01 and leave this register at 0.
With mono mode off, bit 1 set makes each timer tick fetch a left and then a right sample; clear, successive ticks alternate.
On a PAS 16 with bit 1 set and a nonzero prescale divider, the sample clock is 441000 or 1008000 Hz, divided by the divider.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns 0xFF.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns without storing.
Offset 0x8002 reads and writes element 2 of the four-byte system configuration array.
A read returns the byte last written to it.
A write stores the byte and updates the PCM channel.
For a PAS 16 with register 0 bit 1 set and a nonzero divider, bit 1 selects 1008000 Hz and clear 441000 Hz, both divided by the divider.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns 0xFF.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns without storing.
Offset 0x8003 reads and writes element 3 of the four-byte system configuration array.
A read returns the byte last written to it.
A write stores the byte and does nothing else with it.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns 0xFF.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns without storing.
Offset 0xF000 reads and writes element 0 of the io_conf array; the source calls its bit 6 the joystick enable.
A read returns the byte last written to it.
A write stores the byte; the source notes that bit 6, the joystick enable, leaves DOSBox-X's joystick unchanged.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns 0xFF.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns without storing.
Offset 0xF001 reads and writes element 1 of the io_conf array and selects the DMA channel.
A read returns the byte last written to it.
A write stores the byte and selects the DMA channel from its low three bits through the table.
Power-up sets the register to 0x03 and the DMA channel to 3.
The table's 4 leaves the card with no DMA channel.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns without storing.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns 0xFF.
Offset 0xF002 reads and writes element 2 of the io_conf array, whose low four bits set the IRQ.
A read returns the byte last written to it.
A write stores the byte, lowers the IRQ, and converts the low four bits to an IRQ number through the converter.
Power-up loads 0x07 with IRQ 10 on the PAS 16, and 0x04 with IRQ 5 on the Plus.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns 0xFF.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns without storing.
Offset 0xF003 reads and writes element 3 of the io_conf array.
A read returns the byte last written to it.
A write stores the byte and does nothing else with it.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns 0xFF.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns without storing.
Offset 0xF400 holds the Sound Blaster and MPU-401 emulation control bits.
A read returns the stored byte with bit 2 reporting a pending Sound Blaster interrupt.
A write keeps bits 7 through 4 and 1 through 0, and applies the Sound Blaster compatibility.
Bit 1 enables the Sound Blaster emulation; the source notes that bit 0 leaves DOSBox-X's own MPU-401 setting unchanged.
Power-up enables the Sound Blaster emulation with the byte 0x02.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns 0xFF.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns without storing.
Offset 0xF401 holds a byte from which the Sound Blaster base is derived.
A read returns the byte last written to it.
A write stores the byte and sets the Sound Blaster base to 0x200 plus its low nibble shifted left four, then applies the compatibility.
Power-up sets the stored byte to 0x30 or-ed with bits 7 through 4 of the configured base.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns 0xFF.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns without storing.
Offset 0xF802 holds a byte that selects the Sound Blaster emulation's IRQ and DMA.
A read returns the byte last written to it.
A write stores the byte, takes an IRQ index from bits 5 through 3, zero meaning none, and the DMA channel from bits 7 and 6.
Power-up encodes the configured Sound Blaster IRQ and DMA into the register.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns 0xFF.
On the original PAS, an offset that reaches this block outside the YM3802 ranges returns without storing.
